tasks.short: Watch the press, catch jams, and adjust it.

steps.what: Observe automatic machines and products for malfunctions.
Decide which adjustments the specifications require.
Make the adjustments on the machine by hand.

tasks.design: She watches the press and the parts and makes the adjustment herself. No jam alert is raised and no setting is sent to the press.
tasks.previous_blocker: A jam and a bad part are seen at the machine. A counter does not show a warped shot or a stuck gate.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the need to stand at the press.
tasks.still_hard: Clearing a jam and choosing the adjustment stay in her hands.
tasks.human_edge: She hears a change in the press and sees a short shot before a counter would.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still watches the press and makes the adjustment.

reach.role: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
reach.task: Check a molded part against the specification before it leaves the press.
reach.learn: Which surface faults are scrap and which are still in tolerance.

evidence.claim: Watching molded parts and clearing a jam stay with the operator. Model knowledge, E1. No plant-efficiency figure is used as her time saving.

assumptions: No system is added, so focal upkeep on this task is zero.
She produces the adjustment decision in s2 from what she saw in s1. No feed and no alert exist for this task.
unknowns: Whether this press exposes a jam signal she already trusts.
research_questions: Which faults does she catch only by looking at the part?

incremental.description: No system is added, so there is no upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still watches every round and still clears every jam, so the saving on this task is zero on a quiet shift and on a shift full of stops.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read specs and plan molding temperatures and sequence.

steps.what: Read specifications and blueprints for this part.
Fill temperatures and settings onto the setup card.
Check temperatures against the plastic materials specified.
Plan the production sequences for the shift.

tasks.design: For a repeat part, {OPS_SYSTEM} fills a setup card from the stored recipe: part number, material, melt temperature, mold temperature, injection pressure, hold, cooling and cycle time. She checks that card against the drawing and plans the sequence. Nothing is sent to the press and nothing is posted to {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Temperatures lived on a paper process sheet, so a card could not be filled until someone had typed the recipe.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored recipe for a repeat part can be copied onto the card without retyping.
tasks.still_hard: A new mold or a new resin has no recipe, and the drawing still needs her.
tasks.human_edge: She knows this mold flashes when the melt is only a little hot.
tasks.altitude: She still reads the drawing and sets the sequence. She can reject a setup card whose temperatures do not match this resin.

reach.task: Read a setup sheet and decide the feeds before cutting.
reach.learn: How a stored setting is checked against the part, not trusted because the part number matched.

evidence.claim: Copying a stored melt temperature onto a setup card is clerical. Reading the drawing and choosing the sequence stay with her. Model knowledge, E1. No measured molding saving is used.
Gear-calculation software sizes gears to published standards. It does not supply molding temperatures, so it is not used here.

assumptions: The recipe contract is part number, material grade, melt temperature, mold temperature, injection pressure, hold time, cooling time and cycle time. The process engineer stores it in {OPS_SYSTEM}. That upkeep is other-role time, counted below.
If the recipe is missing, s2 does not run and she copies the figures from the paper sheet inside s1, which stays full time. No model reads the drawing.
The setup card is a draft she checks in s3. There is no file step and no send step, because nothing is filed and nothing is sent to the press or to {ERP}.
Checking the card against the resin is already her time in s3.
unknowns: Whether the process engineer already keeps recipes in the operations system.
research_questions: What share of jobs are repeat parts with a complete recipe?

already_counted.description: Checking the filled temperatures against the drawing and the resin is her time in s3.

incremental.description: She tells the process engineer when a stored temperature no longer matches the running mold.
The process engineer keeps the recipe fields current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a new-mold day the recipe is missing, s2 does not run, and the saving is 0. On a repeat-part day the card fill is the only saving, and 8 is the high end while she still reads the drawing and plans the sequence.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read gauges and record temperature, pressure and cycle time.

steps.what: Observe meters and gauges the feed does not cover.
Record temperatures, pressures and cycle times from the press.
Verify logged temperatures and pressures against the gauges.
Write why a pressure or cycle time was off.
Confirm the recorded temperatures and pressures.
File the confirmed temperatures and cycle times.

tasks.design: The press control writes melt temperature, mold temperature, injection pressure and cycle time into a draft shift log in {OPS_SYSTEM}. She verifies those lines against the gauges, adds a reason when one is off, and confirms the log. A separate step then files only the version she confirmed. No out-of-range alert is raised and nothing is posted to {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Gauge figures were copied by hand because the shift log was a paper sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: A connected press already holds temperature, pressure and cycle time, so the copy can be configured.
tasks.still_hard: A gauge can stick while the control still reports a normal value.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a true drift from a dead gauge.

ambition.what: She flags a cycle time that drifted on this shift, instead of waiting for the weekly sheet.

tasks.altitude: She stops copying gauge figures and spends that time on readings that disagree with the log. She accepts the shift log before it is filed.

reach.role: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
reach.task: Record a measured dimension against the tolerance.
reach.learn: Write the reason next to the reading that failed, in words the next shift can act on.

evidence.claim: A machine-monitoring app collects produced quantities and machine statuses from the machine control or by manual entry and assigns them to the workplace. This log uses that pattern, with manual entry when the feed is missing.

At one plant, operators collected production data by hand and a live controller feed replaced that collection. The vendor efficiency figure is a plant result and is not this operator's recording time.
Copying a gauge temperature into a log is clerical. Judging that the gauge matches the press is not. Model knowledge, E1.

Works-council consent applies when machine data tied to an operator login can observe behaviour or performance, and when personal data are processed. This log stores press readings. Consent is in the build because a login could turn those readings into a performance record.
AI that monitors and evaluates workers is high-risk. This log is a deterministic copy of readings, not an evaluation of the operator.

assumptions: The press contract is press id, reading time, melt temperature, mold temperature, injection pressure and cycle time. The press control produces it. Press runtime is not her time.
If the feed is missing, s2 does not run and she writes the figures inside s1, which stays full time. s6 then has nothing new to file.
s1 produces leaks, noise, a stuck gauge, and any reading the sensor skips. s4 produces the reason code and a short note. No model drafts the reason.
s3 checks that the logged melt temperature matches the gauge she saw and that the cycle time matches the press she watched, not only that the fields are filled.
s2 is the log fill and is an ungated draft. s6 is the file and runs only on the version she accepted in s5. No out-of-range alert step exists. No {ERP} send step exists.
The log is not tied to a score of her. Consent time is in the build because a login could make it one.
unknowns: Which presses on this floor expose those three readings.
research_questions: How often is the feed missing for a whole shift?

already_counted.description: Comparing each logged reading with the gauge she saw is her time in s3.

incremental.description: She clears a reading the control sent twice or not at all.

approvals.approved_version: confirmed shift log she accepted in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a press with no feed she writes the figures in s1 and the saving is 0. On a connected press the copy and the file are the saving, and 12 is the high end while she still verifies every round and writes every reason.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and mount the tool for this operation.

steps.what: Read which blades or tools this operation needs.
Select the attachment that matches the operation.
Install the blades or tools and check the seating.

tasks.design: She reads the operation, selects the blade or attachment, and mounts it. No tool list is generated and no mount is recorded for her.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right tool depends on this mold and on how the last mount wore.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new mounts a blade for her.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong mount can damage the mold or injure her.
tasks.human_edge: She feels whether the tool is seated before the press closes.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still chooses the tool and mounts it.

reach.task: Fit a mold insert so it seats without play.
reach.learn: What a seated tool feels like before the press closes.

evidence.claim: Choosing and mounting a blade or attachment stays with the operator. Model knowledge, E1. No kit list is generated for her.

assumptions: No system is added, so focal upkeep on this task is zero.
The work order names the tool. She still selects it and mounts it. No tool list is filled and no mount record is written.
unknowns: Whether a second person checks the mount on this floor.
research_questions: Which operations change tools more than once a shift?

incremental.description: No system is added, so there is no upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still selects the tool and still mounts it, on a one-tool day and on a day with several changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still runs the press. She can accept or reject a filled setup card and a filled shift log before the log is kept. Watching parts, clearing jams, and mounting tools stay as they are.
reach: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
skills_to_grow: Judge a filled reading against the gauge, not against a full field.
Keep a reason code specific enough that the next shift can use it.
role.ambitious_version: She spots a drifting cycle on the same shift and stops the run before a bin of scrap, which today waits for the supervisor's weekly sheet. She still does not hand the press to a model.

job.title: Molding, Coremaking, and Casting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
